This is one rehire, and the plan below brings every system in line with it. No human decision is needed.

**What I found**
- **Workday:** Sofia Okafor is back on her old worker record (WID 3a6b86a7975b54a31497024640332b06). It keeps her employee ID E1021, which matches the policy of reusing the ID for rehires. She is a Software Engineer in Engineering, cost center CC-1000, reporting to Jordan Carter (E1001, active). Her start date is 2026-11-02. It is now 00:04 that day, so giving her access now doesn't break the start-date rule. Her Workday work email is already sofia.okafor@example.com.
- **Identity:** Her prior account acct-9fc9370d still exists. It has the same email address and is linked to this worker record, but it is turned off, has no groups or licences, and its mailbox was converted to a shared one. Policy says a rehire reuses the prior account but does not get old access back, so she gets a new mailbox and only the standard groups for her job: All-Staff, VPN-Users and Eng-Git. None of these is privileged, and the segregation-of-duties check found no conflicts.
- **Finance:** Her old profile is still in place with the wrong details. It shows cost center CC-2000 and Ines Novak (AP Manager, Finance) as expense approver. The Workday cost center maps to CC-1000, so both need changing. Her card is off, and she has no open expense reports and no final pay pending. She wasn't issued a new card, so none is planned.
- **ITSM / Legal:** She has no equipment on record, so a laptop order is needed. She is not under any legal hold.
- **Workday onboarding tasks:** Both are "Not Started". Her work email already matches her account, so nothing needs writing back to Workday. Step 9 marks the account-and-email task complete only after steps 1–5 succeed.
